diffs.diff: maximum supply: part 5.5 V, datasheet reading 5 V
diffs.evidence: TI PCF8574 datasheet (SCPS068), Recommended Operating Conditions: 'VCC Supply voltage 2.5 (min) 6 (max) V'; Absolute Maximum: VCC -0.5 to 6.5 V. The Adafruit #5545 board has no regulator: its pinouts page says 'VIN - This is the power pin. To power the board, give it the same power as the logic level of your microcontroller - i.e. for a 5V micro like Arduino, use 5V, or for a 3V micro like a Feather, use 3V', and SCL/SDA are 'level shifted so you can use 3-5V logic'. So VIN is the chip's VCC; '5V' in the Adafruit text is a nominal logic level, not a maximum rating. The model's 5.5 V cap (5 V nominal +10%) stays inside the chip's 6 V recommended maximum; the second reading's 5 V is the nominal level, not the limit.
